sections.h2: Which Lawrence County offices deal with a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Four offices in Louisa handle the tax year between them, and the PVA and the sheriff list the same Main Cross Street address. Each covers its own step.

  • Property Valuation Administrator (PVA): 122 Main Cross Street, Louisa, KY 41230. The PVA sets the assessed value and takes homestead applications.
  • Sheriff: 122 Main Cross Street, Louisa. Phone (606) 638-4368. The sheriff takes payment.
  • County Clerk: runs the appeals board paperwork and, after April, the sale of unpaid bills. The clerk's site posts the current delinquent list.
  • County Attorney: mails the warning letters to owners whose bills have moved to the clerk.

Taxing districts set different rates, so the sheriff's bill and the PVA's assessment for your own parcel are the figures that count.

sections.h2: What should a Lawrence County owner know about the place?
sections.html:
Lawrence County was formed in 1821 from parts of Floyd and Greenup counties and has had four courthouses over the years. Louisa holds the courthouse and is the one incorporated city. In the east, a quarter-mile concrete T-bridge links Louisa to Fort Gay, West Virginia, across the point where the Levisa Fork and the Tug River join to form the Big Sandy River. Yatesville Lake covers about 2,300 acres, opened in 1992 and is run by the Army Corps of Engineers for flood control and recreation. Alcohol sales are limited to Louisa city limits.

  • People: an estimated 15,765 in July 2025, compared with 16,293 counted in 2020 and 15,860 in 2010. About 416 square miles of land works out to 39 residents per square mile.
  • Housing: 7,737 units and 6,342 households, with 77.8 percent owned by their occupants.
  • Middle home value: $111,700. Typical owner costs are $1,216 a month for mortgaged homes and $386 for paid-off ones, while typical rent is $760.
  • Income: $46,772 for the median household, with 23.4 percent of people in poverty.
  • Work: 207 employer establishments with 2,950 jobs in 2023, a 5.9 percent rise over 2022, and a 30.1 minute average commute.
  • 83.7 percent of households have broadband, and 81.7 percent of adults over 25 finished high school.

sections.h2: What is the payment deadline in Lawrence County, and what happens after it?
sections.html:
Under KRS 134.015 the sheriff wants the money by December 31, and owners who pay everything by November 1 keep 2 percent. January costs 5 percent extra, and February onward costs 10 percent. The state's sample for a $1,000 bill makes the late cost concrete: a $100 penalty plus a $110 sheriff add-on fee, so the bill is about 21 percent higher from February 1, before any commission.

Late-mailed bills fall under a state alternative schedule that allows 30 days per stage. Oil and gas bills also exist in Lawrence County. The clerk's delinquent tax page says its sale leaves out the 2023 oil and gas bills, so ask the sheriff whether one is attached to your parcel.

sections.h2: How does a Lawrence County owner fight a high valuation?
sections.html:
The sequence runs in order. Step one is a sit-down with the PVA's staff. Step two is the May viewing window for the roll. Step three is the written appeal, filed with the clerk by the end of the next workday after viewing, and step four is the hearing before the local board roughly a month on. Only evidence counts at the hearing, so bring proof such as a description of the lot and buildings, insurance papers, construction costs and listings of nearby sales.

Written reasons follow any change the board makes. Hearings may be recorded, and a paid representative has to fit the categories in KRS 133.120. Skipping the board closes off the Kentucky Claims Commission.

sections.h2: Who can claim the Lawrence County homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Eligible owners are those who have turned 65 and those classified as fully disabled. The 2025-26 figure is $49,100 off the assessment, so a house assessed at $150,000 is taxed on $100,900. Locally, 19.9 percent of people are past 65, and 17.5 percent of those younger report a disability.

The PVA's courthouse office takes the form. A claim built on disability has to be renewed each year. Veterans with a service-connected disability are excused, as is anyone Social Security or a state retirement system has declared permanently and totally disabled.

sections.h2: How has Lawrence County's head count changed over time?
sections.html:
Lawrence County reached 20,067 people in 1910, dropped to 10,726 by 1970, then climbed back to 14,121 in 1980 and has stayed between roughly 14,000 and 16,300 since. The 2020 census counted 16,293 residents. The July 2025 estimate of 15,765 sits about 3 percent under the 2020 base.

The same Census tables show 6,342 households, 612 veterans, and a labor force participation rate of 46.7 percent. Retail sales came to about $209 million in 2022 and health care receipts to about $81 million. A seller who needs to confirm the exact bill, the exemption status or a possible lien will find that the offices above can answer in a single visit to Louisa.

sections.h2: How does the Lawrence County Clerk sell unpaid tax bills?
sections.html:
What the sheriff has not collected by April 15 moves to the clerk as certificates of delinquency, and 1 percent monthly interest begins. County attorney letters go out, and the clerk advertises the list ahead of the sale. A registered outside buyer can take over the lien at the sale, and the owner then owes the money to that buyer. The Lawrence County Clerk's website lays out how its draft-style sale works, which also tells an owner how much the buyer may be paying.

Lawrence County Clerk delinquent tax sale rules (lawrencekyclerk.com, delinquent taxes page)
ItemRule
RegistrationAt least 10 business days before the sale
Deposit$10 per bill, capped at $250, not refundable
Prior year certificatesSeparate list due 10 business days before the sale
Bidders per entityOne potential purchaser
Order of purchaseRandom drawing, lowest number picks first, in rounds
PaymentCash, certified check, money order or company check
RefundsNone after the sale

The lien on the land from delinquent taxes lasts eleven years under KRS 134.015, no matter who owns the property.

sections.h2: What should a Lawrence County seller handle before listing?
sections.html:
• Ask the sheriff at (606) 638-4368 for the current bill and any earlier unpaid year.
  • Check the clerk's delinquent list to see whether a certificate already exists on the parcel.
  • Holders of the homestead exemption should ask the PVA what happens to it at a sale.
  • Compare your assessment with the sales of similar houses before the May inspection window opens, in case a dispute is worth filing.
  • Agree on the split of the current bill in the sales contract.

Owners who want no repairs or showings can request a direct offer. Unpaid tax is settled from the proceeds at closing either way.

faqs.q: Where is the Lawrence County tax bill paid?
faqs.a: The Lawrence County Sheriff collects it at 122 Main Cross Street in Louisa. Call (606) 638-4368 to confirm the amount and the payment methods before you go.

faqs.q: How much does paying early save in Lawrence County?
faqs.a: Two percent, if the bill is paid in full by November 1. KRS 134.015 sets that discount, and the printed amount applies from November 2 through December 31.

faqs.q: What comes first when disputing a value here?
faqs.a: Meet with the PVA or a deputy. The local board of assessment appeals will not hear an owner who has not had that conference first.

faqs.q: How big is the homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It removes $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. Owners must be 65 or older or classified as totally disabled, and the PVA takes the application.

faqs.q: Can an outside buyer purchase an unpaid bill here?
faqs.a: Yes. If a certificate of delinquency is unpaid at the clerk's sale, a registered third party purchaser can buy the lien, and the owner then pays that buyer.
